name: contradictory-answers
description: The user answered yes to storing card numbers and yes to a hosted payment page that keeps card data off the servers. The analyst must raise the conflict as a blocking question, not pick a side or declare readiness.

configuration.name: Maker Market
configuration.description: A storefront for handmade goods with a cart and checkout.

context.goal: Let makers sell handmade goods online.

requirements.statement: Shoppers can add products to a cart and pay at checkout.
acceptance_criteria: A shopper completes a test purchase.

questions.prompt: Will the shop store customers' card numbers itself?
Must checkout use a hosted payment page so card data never touches your servers?

context.goal: Let makers sell handmade goods online.

questions.prompt: Your answers conflict: storing card numbers yourself puts your servers in full PCI DSS scope, while a hosted payment page keeps card data off them. Which should the shop do?
questions.why: This decides the payment architecture and the security obligations.
options: Use a hosted payment page and never store card numbers
Store card numbers ourselves and take on full PCI DSS compliance

blockers: The answers to DQ-001 and DQ-002 conflict.

decisions: Raised the conflict between DQ-001 and DQ-002 instead of choosing one side.
